summary: Andrew J. Nicholson is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under the traditional teacher Shrinarayan Mishra. He held a post at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served at the Insight Meditation Society, the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and the Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University, learning under Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, John Pemberton, D. Dennis Hudson, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Alan Sponberg, and Richard Rorty.

Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2015).

Andrew Sihler worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard (~1958–1962) and Yale (~1963–1967) under Warren Cowgill, later holding a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1967–2002).
Andrew Watsky is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1985–1994), and he held a post at Vassar College (~1994–2008).
Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006), where he was supervised by Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA (-2010) and PhD (-2016) at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and other scholars, later becoming a professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

Andrey Terentyev is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University's Faculty of Philosophy (~1970–1975) and worked at the Museum of History of Religion (~1978–1991).

Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902–1906) and Leipzig University (~1903–1906). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and the University of Lviv (1917).

András Róna-Tas works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, later holding posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Szeged (1968–2002), and the University of Vienna.

André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France, with supervisors including Jean Filliozat. He held posts at the CNRS (1947–1951), EPHE (1956–1973), and Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Caquot was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and EPHE, he held posts at EPHE (~1955–1992), the University of Strasbourg (1957–1960), the University of Paris (1964–1968), and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965–1971), EPHE (~1972–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972–1977), later holding a post at Laval University (~1980–2010).

André Godard was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts (~1899–1905) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934–1960).

André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne (~1926–1937) and Humboldt University of Berlin, mentored by Antoine Meillet. He held posts at EPHE (~1938–1947), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1978).
André Mazon was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1901–1904) and Charles University (~1904–1905). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris under mentors including Louis Renou and Swami Lakshman Joo. He directed the Institut Français de Francfort (~1959–1964) and held posts at the CNRS.
André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctorate under August Conrady (~1908–1912) and served at Leipzig University (~1917–1945).

Andy Rotman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago, supervised by Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, and held a post at Smith College (attested 2013–2017).
